scope: Build-facing design requirements for the next JNAP template round and future client personal PR templates.

requirements.title: Mobile and experience first
requirements.description: Every template must start from the mobile path through the site, then scale to desktop without compressing or overexplaining the content.
acceptance_checks: Primary exits are reachable in the first mobile viewport.
Tap targets meet or exceed local 44px design-object requirements.
Desktop layout is an expansion of the mobile experience, not a separate pitch page.
anti_goals: Desktop-first decorative composition.
Hero copy required to explain the navigation.

requirements.title: Curiosity with clear exits
requirements.description: The root should make visitors want to interact further while keeping the useful exits obvious.
acceptance_checks: The first screen gives a clear read of identity and at least two next actions.
At least one below-fold hint is visible on common mobile viewports.
Interaction never hides or delays route access.
anti_goals: Mystery navigation.
Explaining every route on the root.

requirements.title: Show, do not claim
requirements.description: Credibility should come from routes, objects, proof, and specificity instead of generic claims about work or personality.
acceptance_checks: No generic pitch-deck value proposition is required above the fold.
Proof routes are visible as objects or direct links.
Labels stay concrete and plain.
anti_goals: Work, writing, systems, experiments as decorative category language.
Sycophantic or jargony positioning copy.

requirements.title: Personal and professional overlap
requirements.description: The root should feel like one real public identity where professional proof and personal texture coexist under privacy controls.
acceptance_checks: Professional and personal routes can coexist without separate landing pages.
Optional lifestyle modules remain inactive until public review.
Social routes support the person without dominating the site.
anti_goals: Raw social feed mirroring.
Private life as brand content.

requirements.title: Privacy-reviewed personal texture
requirements.description: Lifestyle, photo, social-media, and location-adjacent modules require explicit review before activation.
acceptance_checks: Contracts list privacy review requirements for personal modules.
No private routes, photos, feeds, direct links, or environment values appear in public templates.
Unreviewed personal modules stay planned or disabled.
anti_goals: Using private assets to make the page feel more personal.
Accidental direct-link or provider-data exposure.

requirements.title: Garden-ready docs and wiki
requirements.description: The docs/wiki path should be prepared for exploratory, evolving, connected knowledge rather than a reverse-chronological blog only.
acceptance_checks: Docs/wiki references are treated as deeper routes, not root-page explanations.
Future garden modules can expose state, links, and content maturity.
Navigation provides enough signposts to explore without getting lost.
anti_goals: Decorative garden language without information architecture.
Chronological blog assumptions baked into the root.

requirements.title: Motion as craft, not dependency
requirements.description: Motion may create delight and brand signal, but the static structure must carry all meaning.
acceptance_checks: prefers-reduced-motion behavior exists when animation is used.
No animation is required to find links or understand grouping.
Motion is limited to interaction response, light entrance states, or optional prototypes.
anti_goals: Scroll spectacle.
Autoplay sequences that delay route access.

requirements.title: Template-owned presentation
requirements.description: Spacing, typography, layout, background, density, and motion choices belong to the template unless promoted into shared controls.
acceptance_checks: Shared content remains universal across templates.
Template-specific design decisions live in template folders, control maps, design objects, and tokens.
Candidate templates can be previewed without changing production active-template config.
anti_goals: Current-template spacing baked into site.json.
CSS-only design decisions with no contract or object representation.

requirements.title: Scalable client template system
requirements.description: The design workflow should be reusable for future people and small businesses, not just Justin's root.
acceptance_checks: Pitch artifacts cite bibliography, user stories, and requirements.
Readable Markdown summaries can be generated or maintained for nontechnical review.
Template choices can be compared through preview routes and design objects.
anti_goals: A one-off personal site workflow that cannot become a client product.
Design rationale stored only in chat history.

requirements.title: Contract-first handoff
requirements.description: Agentic design and build work must start from machine-readable contracts with auditable source IDs before implementation.
acceptance_checks: npm run design:validate checks bibliography, user-story, requirement, pitch, one-pager, build-plan, design-object, and token artifacts.
Execplan templates require research inputs for pitch work.
Autonomous build agents stop on missing or invalid research references.
anti_goals: Agents guessing design direction from screenshots only.
Manual reconciliation branches for missing research metadata.
